addresses: BLOCKER, visual-phone: the notice tells Dana that Marcus changed Last name and Grade and never tells her what to. The boxes sit prefilled with the stale upstream values and Save is live, so an untouched box patches his correction back out.
visual-desktop: 'Put the incoming value in the hint that already exists.' The Birthday field already does exactly this ('14 March 2011 — already what Planning Center holds').
changes.change: The two hints now carry the value, in the pattern the Birthday field already uses: '▪ Marcus is changing this to **Chen-Ito**, 40s ago.' and '▪ Marcus is changing this to **10th grade**, 40s ago.' The incoming value is bolded to ink-100, the same emphasis the notice above already uses for field names. The notice's closing clause stopped being a warning about an unknown and became a description of the form: '…Nothing here is locked, and nothing of his is lost: **each of those boxes says underneath what he is changing it to**, and Save sends only the boxes you change.' No new object, no new width, nothing disabled.
changes.rationale: The hint slot was already spending itself on a sentence that named the field the reader was looking at. Putting the value there is the smallest edit that turns J5's forbidden state — typing over something you cannot see — into an informed one. The second half of the fix is a payload rule, not a picture, so it is written into `implementation` rather than drawn: telling the leader 'Save sends only the boxes you change' is only honest if the queue actually behaves that way, and that behaviour is what makes an untouched box safe.
changes.breakpoint: both — the sheet is one column at 390px and 544px alike, and the hint is the same element
changes.implementation: `StudentEditorDialog` already takes `inFlight?: {fields, actor, queuedAt}`; widen it to `inFlight?: {actor, queuedAt, values: Partial}` and render `FormField.hint` as `▪ {actor} is changing this to {formatted value}, {age}.` in `text-warn-400` for each key of `values`. THE PAYLOAD HALF, which is the part that must not be lost: on submit the dialog diffs the form against the snapshot it opened on (`initialValues`, captured once at mount, never re-read while open) and enqueues **only the fields whose value differs**. A queued patch carries a partial, never the whole form. An untouched box is therefore absent from the job document and can never overwrite anybody. This also makes the two-leaders-serial case correct by construction: Marcus's job patches {lastName, grade}, Dana's patches {allergies}, and neither names a field the other typed.

addresses: MAJOR, all four critics: hue sorts the states by the wrong question. `differs` wears the running amber and is counted in 'In flight', so the one row that will never resolve itself is filed with the three that will.

MAJOR, visual-desktop: 'At the end of her four minutes Dana reads In flight 0 · Saves failed 0 and concludes all nine landed, while one record is asserting the church office's value over her correction.'
design-desktop: 'the routine states have been given the longest words, so the physically widest mark in the whole table is the one that must read as nothing is wrong.'
changes.change: The family now sorts by the only question a leader asks down forty-five rows — is this mine to do something about? Warn is the running states and nothing else (queued, sending, waiting, stalled); present is landed; **danger is every state that needs a human — `differs`, `failed`, `orphaned`**; ink is a standing fact with no job behind it. Priya Raman's '≠ Changed upstream · 2m' moved from `uxr-job-run` to `uxr-job-bad`. The counts were cut to the same three buckets: 'In flight 3' (Ava queued, Marcus waiting, Sofia sending) and 'Needs you 2' (Priya differs, Benson failed), replacing 'In flight 4 / Saves failed 1'. The long routine words were shortened so the loudest mark is no longer the calmest state: 'Waiting on a rate limit · 1m' → 'Waiting · 1m', 'Save failed · 1 wk ago' → 'Save failed · 1wk', 'Not in Planning Center yet' → 'No record yet'.
changes.rationale: The journey brief's colour rule leaves four hues, so the separation had to come from re-reading what red means rather than from a fifth. Red now means 'yours to resolve', not 'something broke' — which is true of failed, true of orphaned, and true of differs, where nothing failed but nobody but Dana can say which value is right. That is a semantic shift and it is deliberate: it is the only reading under which the marks and the counts cut the list the same way. The alternative the phone critic floated — leave differs amber and give it a count of its own — keeps the colour lying at row level, where the reader looks first.
changes.breakpoint: both — one tone per state at every width; only the type size steps (12px below lg, 11px at lg), which round 1 set
changes.implementation: In the `JobChip` tone map, move `differs` from the `run` tone to the `bad` tone: `needsAHuman = state in {differs, failed, orphaned}` is now the single predicate that drives the chip tone, the record strip's tone, and the `Edit profile` variant step-down that round 1 introduced. `StudentsPage` quick filters become two job pills from one grouped query: `inFlight = count(state in {queued, sending, waiting, stalled})` with `countTone='warn'`, `needsYou = count(state in {differs, failed, orphaned})` with `countTone='danger'`. There must not be a job state that is reachable by neither pill.

addresses: MAJOR, design-desktop / design-phone: 'six glyphs for nine states, and two of them are doubled onto pairs that must never be read as each other'; '⚠ is already the app's standing mark for allergies'; '‖ means waiting here and held on the outage screen'; '◌ means both queued and no upstream record'.
design-desktop: 'at 11px ◌ and ◷ are both simply small rings — the quarter-fill that separates them is roughly two pixels'.
changes.change: One mark per state, checked at size rather than in a font table: ▪ queued (a solid block — written down), → sending and stalled (an arrow — on its way), ‖ waiting (two bars — paused, resumes), ✓ landed, ≠ differs, ! failed and held (the same state, said once on the group when there are ten of them), ⊘ orphaned, ◌ no upstream record. ◌ now means only 'there is no Planning Center record'; queued took ▪. ‖ now means only 'rate-limited, resumes on its own'; the nine held rows on sync-outage took !, which is honest because a held job *is* a failed job. ⚠ was removed from the family entirely and belongs to the standing Allergy badge again — it appears in these eight files exactly twice, on Ava's and Priya's allergy chips. Verified at 6× on the rendered fold: solid block / arrow / two bars / check / stacked-slash / exclamation / open ring are seven silhouettes, not seven characters.
changes.rationale: The glyph was introduced in round 1 to spare a dim corridor from resolving an 11px word, and it can only do that if the silhouettes are far apart and each one means one thing. The two collisions the critics found were both semantic (a mark that says 'this fixes itself' on a screen where nothing will) rather than cosmetic, so they had to be split rather than restyled. I picked marks by silhouette class first and by metaphor second, which is why sending is an arrow and not another ring.
changes.breakpoint: both — the glyph is identical at every width; it is the word beside it that shortens below lg
changes.implementation: One `GLYPH: Record<JobState, string>` map beside the tone map in `JobChip`, and nothing else in the app may emit these characters. `stalled` shares `sending`'s arrow deliberately — it is the same job, past a threshold. Add a lint-level rule of thumb for the next person: before adding a mark, check it against `StudentFlagChip`'s set (⚠ is spoken for).

addresses: MAJOR, visual-desktop (sync-outage): 'all nine held rows truncate, and what is cut is always the tail: the author's surname and the time. She cannot tell her own held edits from Marcus's without opening nine records.'

MINOR, design-desktop: 'the marks all start at a fixed x, which reads as a column; the caption is simply flexed in after whatever width the mark happened to need, so its left edge lands in seven different places.'
changes.change: The middle band became two columns instead of a mark with text spilling out of it: the mark sits in a `min-w-40` (160px) slot and the caption starts at a set x. The width for that came off two over-reserved neighbours rather than off the caption — the fixed right-hand flag cluster went `lg:min-w-80` → `lg:min-w-60` (320px → 240px, which is exactly its busiest row's content) and the name column went `lg:w-72` → `lg:w-64` (288px → 256px, still 32px clear of 'Marcus Delacroix-Oyelaran'). On sync-outage all ten captions now render in full — 'Last name, grade · you · Mon 09:41', 'Grade · Marcus Webb · Mon 09:55' — where every one of them was ellipsed before. On sync-students six of seven caption edges are now flush; Amara's caption was shortened to 'Quick-added by Marcus Webb' so it fits.
changes.rationale: The truncation and the ragged edge are the same bug — a row that spends its width on a fixed cluster that is empty on most rows. Fixing the reservation fixes both, and it is a change the implementation has to make anyway because it is a `w-` class on a flex child. I did not take the width from the caption's own column, which is what a `truncate` fix would have done.
changes.breakpoint: at lg and up only — below lg the mark is in the row's chip line with the short word and no caption, exactly as round 1 left it
changes.implementation: `StudentRow`, lg layout: name `lg:w-64`, middle band `{field} · {actor} · {when}`, flag cluster `lg:min-w-60`. The `min-w-40` is a floor, not a cap: a mark longer than 160px ('Changed upstream · 2m') still extends, and that is correct — a mark must never be clipped.

addresses: MAJOR, visual-desktop + visual-phone: 'the default is the destructive one' — Send mine again is the filled brand pill and Keep theirs is 14px grey text, so the overwrite of a named human's deliberate correction is what gets tapped.
MAJOR, visual-desktop: 'two incompatible histories in one sentence. If hers landed at 9:12 and theirs went in at 9:08, the record would hold hers.'

MINOR, design-desktop + design-phone: the two-up is the quietest thing in the strip; labels out-shout values; 'PLANNING CENTER HOLDS' wraps so the two values sit on different baselines; neither cell is marked as the live one; the pair stops short of the strip's right edge.
changes.change: Four things, one strip. (1) Neither move is the default: 'Keep Ito' and 'Send Chen-Ito again' are two matched ink-800 secondaries at the same width, stacked, and the page carries no brand pill in this state at all. The labels name the values so the choice is legible without re-reading the paragraph. (2) One history, in order, with a clock on both sides: 'You typed Chen-Ito at 9:05. At 9:08 the church office changed the same field to Ito. Your edit went out at 9:12, read their value first and left it alone — nothing of yours was written, and nothing of theirs was lost. Which one is right is yours to say.' (3) The two-up was rebuilt: matched single-line labels ('ON THE RECORD NOW' / 'YOU TYPED'), values as the figure at 18px semibold ink-50 against 11px tracked ink-400 labels, one baseline, a provenance line under each ('the church office · 9:08' / 'you · 9:05'), and the live cell ringed in danger with the label that says so. It now spans the strip's full width as its own row, so the bottom-right quadrant is no longer empty. (4) The strip is danger, not warn, matching the row mark. On the phone the comparison sits above the two buttons — the question before the answer.
changes.rationale: The critics agreed on the diagnosis and split on the fix (make Keep theirs primary vs. make them equal). Equal is right: promoting 'Keep theirs' would be Tally asserting that the office is more likely correct, which it does not know either. Two matched secondaries inside a red panel read as a question, which is what this screen is. Naming the values in the buttons is what lets the pair be resolved in a glance instead of a paragraph — it also removes the 'mine/theirs' framing, which was quietly arguing for one side.
changes.breakpoint: both. The order differs: at lg the message and the two actions sit side by side with the comparison full-width beneath (`lg:order-1 / lg:order-2 / lg:order-3` plus `lg:w-full` on the pair); below lg it is message → comparison → the two choices, so the phone reader sees both values before either button.
changes.implementation: `StudentSyncStrip`, `state='differs'`: tone `danger`; render `{requested, observed}` as the two-cell `<dl>` with `ring-danger-500/30` on whichever cell is `observed` (the live one) and an author/time line under each — the drain already records `observedValue` and `observedAt` alongside `requestedAt` when it detects a difference. Both actions use the `secondary` variant; do not pass `variant='primary'` to either. The strip's three children carry `lg:order-1|2|3` and the comparison carries `lg:w-full` so the flex row breaks after the actions. Retiring the job on either action is unchanged, and nothing is persisted as a copy of a managed field — the pair lives on the job and dies with it.

addresses: MAJOR, visual-desktop: 'The frame promises the leader two live fields and shows her none of them' — nothing typeable in the 900px fold, Notes at y≈900 behind the dialog's own clip.
MAJOR, visual-phone: 'Notes is ~500 CSS px below the fold, behind a 295px notice and six boxes that cannot be typed into.'
MINOR, design-desktop + design-phone: the same amber sentence six times becomes the form's dominant rhythm, louder than the notice that explains it and louder than the one move the scene exists for.
MINOR, design-phone: 'the values themselves are dimmed to exactly the grey the app uses for placeholder text, so a name that is on file is indistinguishable from an empty box.'
changes.change: The form is ordered by what is true. Notes and Status now sit directly under the notice that says they are live — Notes is on the first screen at both widths, roughly 555 CSS px down on the phone instead of 1241, and visible in the desktop fold where nothing typeable was before. The six held fields moved into one bordered group below them, and the reason is said once, on the group: '◌ Planning Center's six fields, held until Amara's record exists. What is shown is what the door recorded; creating her unlocks all six.' The six repeated amber hints are gone (the held controls now point their `aria-describedby` at that one sentence). And a held value is a value again: the held controls keep full opacity and render at ink-300, so 'Amara' and 'Whitfield' are plainly filled and the empty Nickname box beside them is plainly empty.
changes.rationale: Round 1 got the boundary right — the lock stops at Planning Center — and then laid the sheet out as if the boundary did not exist. Ordering by what the primary button can honestly do is the cheapest way to make the promise and the geometry agree, and it does not touch the dialog's width, which stays scope-declined. Saying the reason once turns six alarms into one label; the group's border is what carries 'these six are different' after the amber lines come out.
changes.breakpoint: both — the sheet is one column at 390px and 544px, and the reordering is a DOM order, not a breakpoint
changes.implementation:
`StudentEditorDialog`: when every managed field is held, render `[notice, standingNote, Notes, Status, ]` instead of the ordinary field order — the group is a `
`-shaped div with one `

` and the six `FormField`s inside it. `FormField`'s `heldReason` prop stops emitting a per-field hint and instead sets `aria-describedby` to the group's id, and the held control gets `disabled:opacity-100 disabled:text-ink-300` in place of the blanket `disabled:opacity-50` — that pairing is what keeps a filled locked field distinguishable from an empty one, and it should become the default for every disabled control that carries a value.

addresses: MAJOR, visual-desktop: 'the strip got shorter, not cheaper: the wider the button, the narrower the message. On sync-orphaned a 288px button squeezes the message to 273 CSS px — narrower than the same sentence gets on a 390px phone — seven lines, 29% of the fold.'
MINOR, design-desktop: 'the strip's measure is decided by whichever button happens to sit beside it, and across the scenes it swings from 38 characters to 105.'
MAJOR, visual-desktop: 'the sentence that guards this product's most feared operation is 12px ink-500 ~190px below and ~290px left of the button it describes.'
changes.change: The body was given a measure of its own and the action sized to what was left. The message column is now `lg:min-w-96 lg:max-w-[30rem]` — never narrower than 384px, never wider than 480px, about 55–70 characters on every scene — and the strip row is `lg:flex-wrap`, so when the actions cannot fit beside a message at its floor they drop to their own line instead of squeezing it. sync-orphaned's message went from 273px / 7 lines to 445px / 5 lines; sync-outage's went from ~105 characters a line to ~60. The actions column is capped at `lg:max-w-80` and sits beside the words it belongs to rather than being pushed to the far edge. On sync-orphaned the one-new-person guarantee moved out of the message column and into the actions column, directly above the button that fires it, which is where the phone already had it.
changes.rationale: Two ways to give the body a measure: widen the strip out of the record column, or stop the actions from eating it. The first would have made the strip wider than the card under it and would have crept toward the two-column record that stays scope-declined; the second is one `flex-wrap` and one `min-w`, and it is the rule the implementer can state in a sentence. The guarantee had to move because a promise about writing to a church's permanent database has to be readable in the same glance as the button that makes it.
changes.breakpoint: at lg and up. Below lg the strip is the stacked full-bleed band round 1 settled and is unchanged; the measure is the phone's own width there.
changes.implementation: `StudentSyncStrip` root `flex flex-col gap-3 rounded-2xl px-4 py-3 ring-1 lg:flex-row lg:flex-wrap lg:items-start lg:gap-4 lg:py-2`; message `flex min-w-0 flex-1 items-start gap-3 lg:min-w-96 lg:max-w-[30rem]`; actions `flex flex-col gap-3 lg:max-w-80 lg:shrink-0 lg:gap-2`. Any guard or consequence sentence renders inside the actions slot above the button it guards, never in the message. This applies to all four record states and to the page-level outage notice — it is one component.

addresses: MAJOR, visual-desktop + visual-phone: 'the primary is a door most readers cannot walk through' — the frame is Dana Ruiz, core team, the sentence says the fix belongs to an admin, and the loudest object sends her into an admin-gated settings card. 'The brief's own wording for this class is It names an admin — this one names the noun, not a person.'
MINOR, design-phone: 'a notice that governs the entire screen arrives fourth', under a ragged staircase of three secondary buttons, and groups downward with Search.
MINOR, visual-desktop: 'Amara's create is held by the same outage but is dressed as normal progress', with the reason only in a tooltip.
changes.change: The strip names the person: '…**Priya Raman is your admin** — she is the only person who can reconnect it. Nothing typed is lost; all ten go out the moment she does. Retrying will not help.' The primary is now 'Show the 10 held records' — the move a core-team reader can actually make — with 'Tell Priya Raman' as the quiet second; the settings door steps down for this reader and swaps back up when the reader is the admin. The strip also moved above the page header, so a condition of the whole screen arrives first at both widths instead of under three routine buttons. And Amara's create wears the held costume with the rest: '! Create held' in the damped danger tone, her reason on the glass rather than in a `title`, counted in the strip's sentence ('Nine queued edits and Amara Whitfield's new record') and in the pill, which is now 'Held by the outage 10'.
changes.rationale: The aggregation was right and the hand-off was missing — nine edits waiting on a role that the screen would not name. Tally already knows who the admin is, so naming her costs nothing and is the difference between a wall and an errand. Branching the primary on role rather than showing both loudly keeps one loudest object per screen, which is the rule round 1 set for the record strips. Amara had to join the held set because a strip that asserts a scale and then shows a tenth job on the same broken connection as ordinary progress is arguing with itself.
changes.breakpoint: both. The role branch is a data condition, not a viewport one; the strip is the stacked band below lg and the one-line object at lg, as everywhere else.
changes.implementation: `SyncOutageNotice` takes `{heldCount, since, admin: TeamMember | null, viewerIsAdmin: boolean}`. When `viewerIsAdmin` the primary is 'Open Planning Center settings' and 'Show the N held records' is the ghost; otherwise they swap and the ghost becomes 'Tell {admin.firstName} {admin.lastName}' wired to the existing contact path. `admin` comes from the same team query the Team screen uses; if there is no admin, fall back to 'Ask an admin to reconnect it' with no action rather than inventing one. The held count includes pending *creates* on the same failure class, not only patches, and it is the same query the pill uses. Render the notice above `<PageHeader>`, not between it and the filters.

addresses: MINOR, design-desktop: 'stepping the page's own primary down was right, but it has landed the record's routine action and its destructive one on exactly the same object — two ink pills, distinguishable only by reading them. The pair had an order before and now it has none.'
design-desktop: 'the 12px caption explains only Remove from roster but is left-aligned to Edit profile, so it reads as a note on the pair.'
changes.change: 'Remove from roster' became the low-emphasis text button in every state, so there is an order whatever the strip is doing: strip action (loud when the state needs a human) > Edit profile (brand when nothing needs a human, ink pill when something does) > Remove from roster (quiet text). The footnote now sits on its own line under both and was rewritten to name its subject — 'Remove from roster leaves their Planning Center record alone, and keeps every gathering they attended' — so it cannot be read as a note on the pair regardless of where the row wraps.
changes.rationale: The round-1 rule (one loudest object per record) was right and produced a tie one level down. Demoting the destructive action rather than re-promoting Edit profile keeps the rule intact and is also just correct: 'Remove from roster' should never be a same-weight sibling of 'Edit profile' on a screen a leader is moving through quickly. Rewriting the caption was cheaper and more robust than aligning it.
changes.breakpoint: both — the same three ranks at 390px and 1440px
changes.implementation: `StudentDetailPage` actions row: `<Button variant={jobNeedsAHuman ? 'secondary' : 'primary'}>Edit profile</Button>` (unchanged from r01) and `<Button variant='ghost'>Remove from roster</Button>` (was `secondary`). The caption is `<span class="basis-full text-xs text-ink-500">` and its first two words name the button it belongs to. The `ghost` variant is the one added in r01 for 'Discard the edit'.

addresses: MINOR, design-phone: 'four counts, three visible treatments — the danger tint at the same alpha has no luminance against the chip body, so Saves failed renders as a bare red digit with no container. The one number that means somebody's correction was refused is the only one that has lost its shape.'
changes.change: All four counts are one object again: the disc is `bg-ink-800` on every pill and only the numeral carries the hue — ink-400 for neutral, warn-400 for 'In flight', danger-400 for 'Needs you' (and for 'Held by the outage' on sync-outage). The tinted disc fills that had no luminance against the chip body are gone.
changes.rationale: The finding is exactly right and the fix is the smaller of the two available: colouring the container needed a fill that reads on ink-900, which would have made the count louder than the pill it sits in; colouring the digit keeps one shape and four instances, which is what the row is.
changes.implementation: `QuickFilterChip`: the count span is always `rounded-full bg-ink-800 px-1.5 py-0.5 text-[11px] font-semibold tabular-nums` and `countTone` selects only the text colour. Remove the `bg-{tone}-500/20` branch.

addresses: MINOR, visual-desktop + visual-phone: '`stalled` still has no wording. Nothing anywhere says the thing the brief insists on — that a long job may still land — so the inference from 4m is left to the reader.'
The round instruction: stalled needs a sentence, not a scene.
changes.change: `stalled` was given its vocabulary without a frame: it shares `sending`'s mark (→) and differs only by a threshold and a heading. The words are now attached to the sending state on the glass — the sending mark's own description reads 'A server is talking to Planning Center about this one right now. Past about two minutes it reads "Taking longer than it should — it may still land, nothing has failed."' — and the strip copy is written into the implementation below so it survives into `src/`. No new scene, no new mark, no new tone.
changes.rationale: Both desktop critics said the age on the mark took most of the harm out of this and that what remained was one threshold and one heading. A seventh frame would have bought a rendering of a sentence I can simply write down. Sharing the sending mark is deliberate — stalled is not a different job, it is the same job with a clock on it, and giving it a mark of its own would say otherwise.
changes.implementation: `stalled` is derived, not stored: `state === 'sending' && now - job.claimedAt > 120_000`. `JobChip` renders the sending arrow with the word 'Still sending · {age}'. `StudentSyncStrip` renders tone `warn`, heading 'Taking longer than it should', body 'It has been going out for {age}. It may still land — nothing has failed, and nothing you typed is lost.', **no cancel action** (the job is claimed). Nothing anywhere may render `stalled` in the danger tone: it is a running state and belongs in the 'In flight' count.

declined.finding: visual-phone (minor): the queued strip's promise is unconditional and the offline case still has no words of its own — Marcus in a basement corridor is told the edit proceeds without him when nothing has left the handset. 'Same object, one extra branch.'
declined.why: Declined as a frame for the second time, and the critic agrees it is survivable ('the cost is a temporarily false belief rather than a lost correction; the editor's stale prefill is the bigger hole'). This round already spends its budget on the blocker, on re-cutting the family, and on three scenes' worth of structure; adding a ninth frame is how the loop stops converging. The branch is small and fully specified in r01 and unchanged: when the write has not been acknowledged by the server, the same strip reads heading 'Held on this phone — no signal', body 'It has not left the device yet. It goes as soon as you have signal, even if you lock the screen', same secondary Cancel, and the row mark is ◌ in the ink tone. If a critic still wants to see it rendered, it is one prop next round.

declined.finding: visual-phone (minor): four of nine states have a phone record frame; `sending` and `waiting` exist only as 12px row chips. 'Cheapest proof is one render of the sending strip carrying its age.'
declined.why: Declined as a frame. The strip is one component with a state switch that four states already demonstrate; a fifth render proves the switch, not the design. The wording for `sending`, `waiting` and `stalled` is written out in the `stalled` change above and in r01, and the age is already proven on the queued strip ('by you 14 seconds ago') and on every row mark. What would be worth a frame is a state whose *shape* is different, and sending's is not.

declined.finding: visual-desktop (minor, second half): 'while an outage notice is standing, the create action in sync-blocked should be visibly held rather than inviting.'
declined.why: Real, and declined because it is a cross-scene state combination rather than a finding about either scene. sync-blocked is Amara's editor in ordinary conditions; making its create button held would mean rendering the outage into a frame that is not about the outage, and the next critic would rightly ask which of the two states the frame is showing. The rule belongs in the implementation and is stated there: any action that enqueues work against the backend renders disabled with the outage's reason while an outage notice is standing, and that includes 'Create her in Planning Center'.

declined.finding: design-desktop (minor, residual): the caption's left edge is still not perfectly flush — 'Changed upstream · 2m' is 178px against a 160px mark slot, so Priya Raman's caption starts 18px right of the other six.
declined.why: Left, deliberately. The slot is a floor rather than a cap because a clipped state mark is worse than a 18px step in a caption edge, and the alternative — sizing the slot to the widest possible mark — would take 40px of caption width off every row on sync-outage, where the caption is the whole point. The spread went from 84px across seven rows to 18px on one. Shortening 'Changed upstream' to fit would cost the reader the one word that says where the change came from.

declined.finding: MINOR, design-desktop: sync-orphaned's strip is still tall — 290px against 258px before, because the wide 'Re-create her in Planning Center' action now drops to its own line.
declined.why: Accepted as the price. The finding it answers was that the message set to 38 characters over seven lines on a 1440px laptop; it is now 55 characters over five, with the one-new-person guarantee adjacent to the button it guards. Buying the 32px back would mean either shortening the action's label (which is the one place the operation is named in full) or reserving a narrow action column again, which is the thing that caused the trench.

declined.finding: r01 scope declines: the two-column record at lg, and a wider editor dialog at lg.
declined.why: Not re-filed and not re-argued, per this round's instruction. They stay declined.
